tieu_de: Jupiter transit through the 7th house: the people who help you grow
mo: Will I get married when Jupiter is in my 7th house?
What if I am already in a relationship?
Can this transit help with legal disputes?

For roughly a year, the most useful thing in your life may be another person. When Jupiter crosses your Descendant into the 7th house, partners, close friends, clients and collaborators come into focus, and many of them bring something good with them.

The 7th house is about one-to-one bonds of every kind: marriage, business partnership, the friend you call first, even the opponent across the table. Jupiter makes these relationships wider, warmer and more rewarding, and it tends to bring in new ones that matter for years afterward.

doan: After six houses focused mostly on you and your private life, Jupiter now crosses the horizon of your chart and turns outward. Growth this year comes through others. You learn from them, lean on them and build things with them that you could not build alone.

The relationships that thrive under this transit tend to be ones where both people grow. It favours a partner who brings out your best and a collaborator who fills your gaps, rather than someone who only makes you comfortable.
Planet Jupiter Rules Sagittarius Expansion, knowledge, luck

You meet someone who opens a door: a mentor, a business partner, a client who becomes a friend. A romantic relationship deepens, and conversations about moving in, getting engaged or marrying come up naturally. An existing partnership starts to feel more generous, with more shared plans and more support.
At work, contracts and joint ventures often go well. Negotiations feel fairer. Even disputes can settle in your favour or end with a sensible compromise.

The main blessing is fortunate people. Someone who enters your life now may support your growth for years, whether as a spouse, a partner in business or a trusted adviser. Knowledge and help flow both ways, and you are likely to give as much as you receive.
This is also a strong time to formalise commitments that are ready. Jupiter supports vows, agreements and partnerships built on shared values.

Jupiter can make you idealise the other person. A new partner looks perfect, a business deal looks foolproof, and you skip the questions you would normally ask. You may also hand over too much, expecting the other person to provide the growth you need to do yourself.
Watch, too, for a habit of saying yes to everyone. Not every offered partnership is a good one, and the generous mood of this year can make it hard to decline.

Jupiter spends about a year in a sign and a similar time in each house. The size of your 7th house depends on the house system and your birth latitude, so the transit may run shorter or longer than a year. The crossing of the Descendant, sometimes repeated through retrograde, often marks the first meeting or decision.
Be available to meet people. Accept introductions, attend events where your future collaborators might be, reply to the message you would normally leave for later.
In romance, notice who makes you want to grow, not just who makes you feel good.
Before signing a partnership or legal agreement, read it with a clear head and ask a trusted third party to look it over.
Give generously to the people who support you. Thank-you notes, shared credit and returned favours strengthen these bonds.
Keep some of your own goals in view so the relationship adds to your life rather than replacing it.

Marriage and serious commitments are common under this transit, but it is not a guarantee. What Jupiter reliably brings is growth through a close relationship, and for some people that means a wedding, for others a business partnership or a deep friendship.

The transit often renews it. Couples tend to plan more together, travel, learn from each other or take a next step. If the relationship has been struggling, this is a good year to seek help and give it a fair chance.
The 7th house includes open opponents, and Jupiter tends to favour fair settlements. It still pays to be well prepared and well advised, since optimism is not a legal strategy.
